name: Chunchali Beel
short_description: A quiet birding backwater where locals fish at dawn — no crowds, just herons, egrets and morning mist.
why_hidden: Not on any tour circuit; reached by a village track most drivers don't know. Best experienced with a local who fishes there.
how_to_reach: ~20 min by bike/auto from Kamalabari ghat on Majuli; ask for the Chunchali fishing point.
embedding_text: Chunchali Beel is a quiet birding backwater wetland near Majuli. Locals fish at dawn. Herons, egrets, migratory waterfowl, mist. No crowds, offbeat, hidden lake for birdwatching.

name: Salmara Sandbar
short_description: A sunset point on a shifting Brahmaputra sandbar, reachable only by country boat — known mostly to Majuli's ferrymen.
why_hidden: The sandbar moves with the river each year, so it's never marked; you need a boatman who knows this season's channel.
how_to_reach: Country boat from Salmara ghat, ~30 min; arrange the evening before with a local ferryman.
embedding_text: Salmara Sandbar is a Brahmaputra river sandbar sunset viewpoint near Majuli, reachable only by country boat. Ferrymen know it. Remote, offbeat, hidden island, golden hour, river.

name: Kamalabari Pottery Lane
short_description: Hand-thrown clay pots made the same way for 500 years, one family workshop at a time — coiled and beaten by hand, no wheel.
why_hidden: The potters don't advertise; visitors usually only see the finished pots in markets, not the lane where they're made.
how_to_reach: Kamalabari town on Majuli, behind the main road near the Satra; ask for the kumar (potter) para.
best_time: Year-round mornings; avoid peak monsoon when firing stops
embedding_text: Kamalabari Pottery Lane on Majuli is a traditional potters' quarter. Hand-built coiled clay pots, 500-year-old technique, family workshops, Assamese craft, artisan, heritage, hidden.

name: Dhodar Ali roadside tea shacks
short_description: The unmarked bamboo tea shacks along the old Dhodar Ali road where estate workers stop — red tea, boiled eggs, and gossip.
why_hidden: Tourists are driven straight to the manicured estate bungalows; the actual tea culture is on the roadside.
how_to_reach: Anywhere along Dhodar Ali between Jorhat and Titabor; look for the crowd of bicycles.
best_time: Early morning or 4pm, when shifts change
embedding_text: Dhodar Ali roadside tea shacks near Jorhat serve strong red Assam tea to tea-garden workers. Authentic tea culture, cha, offbeat food stop, local life, hidden.

name: Sivasagar home kitchens (Tai-Ahom food)
short_description: A handful of Sivasagar families cook Tai-Ahom meals — khar, xaak, fish in banana leaf — for guests who ask ahead.
why_hidden: It's a word-of-mouth home-dining network, not restaurants; you have to be introduced.
how_to_reach: Arranged through a local guide in Sivasagar, usually a day's notice.
embedding_text: Sivasagar Tai-Ahom home-cooked meals: khar, xaak, patot diya maas. Home dining, food experience, Ahom heritage cuisine, offbeat, hidden, local family.

name: Hoollongapar edge-trail at dawn
short_description: Standing at the forest edge of Hoollongapar just after 5am to hear the hoolock gibbons' territorial calls roll across the canopy before the day-trippers arrive.
why_hidden: Most visitors come mid-morning for the walk; the dawn sound experience needs an early permit and a forest guard willing to open the gate.
how_to_reach: Hoollongapar Gibbon Sanctuary gate near Mariani; arrange the pre-dawn slot with the range office the day before.
embedding_text: Hoollongapar Gibbon Sanctuary dawn trail near Jorhat. Hoolock gibbon calls at first light, canopy, primates, birdsong, quiet, offbeat wildlife, hidden.
